proof_nl:
Because 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, the integers a, b, r+a, and r+b are all nonnegative, so every q-Pochhammer symbol appearing in the claimed identity is defined.

First consider the case a = b. By the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q), the product from i = a+1 to b is empty, so P_{a,b,r}(q) = 1. On the other hand,
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_a)
= 1.
So the identity holds when a = b.

Now assume a < b. We use the following elementary consequence of the definition of (q;q)_n: for any nonnegative integers m < n,
(q;q)_n = (q;q)_m \prod_{j=m+1}^n (1 - q^j).
Indeed, if m = 0 then this is just (q;q)_n = 1 \cdot \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j), using (q;q)_0 = 1; if m > 0, it follows by splitting the defining product for (q;q)_n after the factor j = m.

Apply this with m = r+a and n = r+b. Since a < b, we have r+a < r+b, so
(q;q)_{r+b} = (q;q)_{r+a} \prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j).
Apply it again with m = a and n = b:
(q;q)_b = (q;q)_a \prod_{j=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^j).

Since each factor 1 - q^j is a nonzero polynomial, these products are invertible in the rational function field Z(q). Therefore,
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= \frac{\prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j)}{\prod_{j=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^j)}.

Now reindex the numerator by writing j = r+i. As j runs from r+a+1 to r+b, the index i runs from a+1 to b. Hence
\prod_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j) = \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i}).
Substituting this gives
((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
= \frac{\prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i})}{\prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^i)}
= \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} \frac{1 - q^{r+i}}{1 - q^i}
= P_{a,b,r}(q),
where the last equality is exactly the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q).

Thus, in all cases,
P_{a,b,r}(q) = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b)
in the rational function field Z(q).

domain_restrictions: a, b, and r are integers
a and b satisfy 0 <= a <= b
q is not a numeric value but an indeterminate
n is restricted to nonnegative integers in the definition of q-Pochhammer
The product defining P runs over integers i from a + 1 to b inclusive
When a = b, the product defining P is the empty product and equals 1
When n = 0, the q-Pochhammer symbol equals 1
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer triple a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if P of a, b, r at q is defined as the product over i from a + 1 to b of (1 minus q to the power r plus i) divided by (1 minus q to the power i), with empty product equal to 1 when a = b, and if q-Pochhammer n is defined for nonnegative n as the product over j from 1 to n of (1 minus q to the power j), with value 1 at n = 0, then P of a, b, r at q equals the ratio of q-Pochhammer terms: q-Pochhammer at r + b times q-Pochhammer at a divided by q-Pochhammer at r + a times q-Pochhammer at b, as an identity of rational functions.
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0
For each nonnegative integer n, define the q-Pochhammer symbol
Then the stated identity holds in the rational function field over the integers

statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate and define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when a = b. For each nonnegative integer n, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j), with (q;q)_0 := 1. Then one has the identity in the rational function field Z(q): P_{a,b,r}(q) = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b).

status_snapshot.last_transition_reason: The proof establishes exactly the claimed q-Pochhammer identity. It correctly separates the empty-product case a = b, then for a < b expands (q;q)_{r+b} and (q;q)_b relative to (q;q)_{r+a} and (q;q)_a, cancels in the rational function field, reindexes the numerator product, and matches the definition of P_{a,b,r}(q). This aligns with the lemma sketch and its role as a product-to-factorial-ratio rewrite. No undeclared or forbidden dependencies are used.
